description_top: Forty engineers, five teams, six months. How do you split the work so the teams can move independently, and what do you own as the manager? A full reference solution at the principal and senior engineering-manager bar: theory first, a three-version team-to-component map, six challenges (the critical path, a late dependency, a shared table, a contract dispute, a lost team, and how you would know the split is wrong). {DURATION} minutes, {SLIDES} numbered slides, with an interviewer, a candidate and a coach.

The thesis: cut along domain seams, put a versioned contract on every seam, give shared things one owner, integrate end to end by week four, and keep the contracts, the dependency graph and the milestones for yourself.

ABOUT THIS VIDEO
This is a scripted walkthrough, not a recording of a real interview, and the interviewer, candidate and coach are not real people. The voices are synthetic (Kokoro-82M, generated locally). Script, diagrams and the written design were produced with Claude Code. Numbers are back-of-the-envelope estimates for the exercise, labelled as illustrative, not any company's real figures. The technical content has not been reviewed by a person.
